newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-PRICE CLINCHES TITLE IN SUN CITY GLOOM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PRICE CLINCHES TITLE IN SUN CITY GLOOM.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Nick Price romped to an eight-stroke victory in the Dimension Data Pro-Am on Sunday as he shot a final round three-under-par 69.

It gave him a 72-hole total of 268 and left him 20-under-par for the tournament which, because of an 80-minute break for an afternoon thunderstorm, ended in near darkness. Some players were forced to run between shots in an effort to finish before the night closed in entirely but it did nothing to upset a serene Price.

South Africa's David Frost was alone in second place on 276, 12 under par, after an up-and-down closing round of 71. One shot further back was Thomas Bjorn of Denmark who finished with a costly bogey-five on the 18th.
The 40-year-old Price, a former world number one, endured a form slump in 1996 because of illness, and this was his first win since the Zimbabwe Open in November 1995.
"The guys on the U.S. tour will say that this win doesn't count because it wasn't over there. But I feel the way I played this week I would have had a good chance to win wherever I played," he said.

"The key to it all was my putting. That's the real reason that I haven't been winning and I don't believe I had a three-putt all week. It was also great to be on the Gary Player Country Club because I just love this golf course".
"In my last three tournaments I've finished third, second and first. Where else can I go from here? I'll probably miss the cut next week!".

Price was paired with Padraig Harrington in the final three-ball, but the talented Irishman struggled all day and ended with a three-over-par 75. He bogeyed the last two holes in the gathering gloom to finish with a group of five players at nine-under-par.
